original_description: Interview the user, one question at a time, before building anything. Use this whenever the user wants to build, add, or change a feature, game, mechanic, tool or app in a code project, especially when the request is short or open-ended ("add a boss fight", "I want a second level", "let's make a todo app", "what if enemies could...?"), or when they say "grill me", "interview me", "help me spec this", or "let's plan this out". Make sure to use it even if the user doesn't ask for a plan, because a request that sounds simple usually hides several design decisions. Do not use it for bug fixes, fully specified small edits, or questions about how existing code works.

Interview them one question at a time, then write DESIGN.md. It applies whatever the wording: a loose one-liner ("make the game harder, your call", "can we add a second level?"), a request that names a stack, an addition to a project that already works well, or an explicit "grill me", "interview me", "help me spec this" or "let's plan this out first". Do not use it for bug fixes, failing tests, tiny fully specified edits like a color or rename, explaining or reviewing existing code, or general questions.

Use it whenever the user asks to add, build, extend or plan something new, even in a single vague sentence, or even when they have already named a stack. Examples are "make the game harder", "add a second level", "let's make a bot" and "I want multiplayer". Use it whenever they ask to spec or plan something, or say "grill me", "interview me" or "plan this out". They may leave decisions to you ("your call"), or they may not mention design at all, but the work still hides unmade choices about scope, behavior and success criteria. Do not use it for bug fixes, failing tests, small fully specified edits such as a color or rename, code explanations, or general questions.
